correctness.rationale: In curvature -1, each geodesic chord on radius-R circle obeys sinh(d/2)=sinh(R)sin u. In a triangle with x=s-a etc, the exact hyperbolic inradius identity tanh r=(1/2) sqrt(prod(1-e^{-2x})/(1-e^{-2s})) implies r<atanh(1/2)=log(3)/2 and yields the fixed-gap scaled limit Z=(1/3) sum(sin^2 U/(sin²V sin²W))=(1/3) sum(cot V+cot W)² as R->infinity. Anchoring at the first labeled sampled vertex gives truly uniform Dirichlet(1,1,1) half-gap simplex density 2/pi²; anchoring at an absolute polar minimum would be different and is explicitly excluded. If m=min(U,V,W), Z<=4/m² implies exceedance requires a shrinking boundary chart. Under U=q/sqrt(t), V=pi h, the indicator 1_{Z>t} converges almost everywhere to 1_{q<sqrt(2/3)} and is uniformly dominated on q<2, h in(0,1). Each of three charts contributes (2/pi)sqrt(2/3)/sqrt(t). The chart densities converge in L1 and thus normalized joint law converges in total variation to independent uniform index, q and residual h; layer cake gives moment cutoff p<1/2. Independently simulated 550,000 Dirichlet half-gap triples: sqrt(t) P(Z>t) was 1.55486,1.54368,1.55698 at t=1000,5000,15000 versus 1.55939 predicted; this finite corroboration was not used as a proof.
